description: A four-row by three-column composite EBSD figure of LDS samples. Columns are inverse pole figure (IPF) maps (left), kernel average misorientation (KAM) maps (centre, colour bar labelled 0°–5°), and grain-boundary (GB) distribution maps (right, legend: blue line = 2–10°, red line = >10°). Rows are the four conditions: (a–a₂) S0, (b–b₂) S950, (c–c₂) S1050, (d–d₂) S1150 per the caption. Row (a) uses 50 µm scale bars; rows (b)–(d) use 100 µm scale bars. Each IPF map carries a colour triangle keyed to [001], [101], [111]. (a) shows a bimodal, non-uniform microstructure — large grains with clusters of fine grains at their interfaces — while (b)–(d) become progressively coarser and more equiaxed, with abundant straight parallel annealing-twin lamellae in (c), (c₂), (d) and (d₂). (a₁) is mottled green/yellow-highlighted, indicating elevated local misorientation, whereas (b₁)–(d₁) are almost uniformly dark blue (low misorientation). (a₂) is dominated by blue LAGB traces; (b₂)–(d₂) are dominated by red HAGB traces that become sparser from (b₂) to (d₂). The multicoloured IPF maps show no dominant colour, i.e. no strong preferred orientation. Together the panels demonstrate that solution treatment homogenizes grain size, removes residual stress, and converts a LAGB-rich structure into a fully recrystallized HAGB/twin-boundary structure whose boundary density falls with rising temperature.

observations.observation: The figure is a 4-row × 3-column composite: each row contains an IPF map, a KAM map with a 0°–5° colour scale, and a GB distribution map with legend '2–10°' (blue) and '>10°' (red).
Row (a) panels carry 50 µm scale bars; rows (b), (c) and (d) carry 100 µm scale bars, and every IPF map includes an IPF colour triangle labelled [001], [101], [111].
The IPF maps of all four conditions are multi-coloured without a dominant orientation colour, indicating no pronounced preferred crystallographic orientation.
Panel (a) (S0) shows a non-uniform, bimodal grain structure with clusters of small grains located at the interfaces of large grains.
Panel (a₁) (S0 KAM) is mottled with green/yellow high-misorientation regions, whereas (b₁), (c₁) and (d₁) are almost uniformly dark blue, i.e. low local misorientation.
Panel (a₂) (S0 GB map) contains a dense population of blue 2–10° LAGB traces, while (b₂), (c₂) and (d₂) are dominated by red >10° HAGB traces.
Grain size increases monotonically in the order (b) S950 < (c) S1050 < (d) S1150, and straight parallel annealing-twin lamellae become more prominent in (c), (c₂), (d) and (d₂).
The boundary networks in (b₂) → (c₂) → (d₂) become progressively sparser as solution temperature rises.
The caption states that (a–a₂), (b–b₂), (c–c₂) and (d–d₂) are the IPF, KAM and GB distribution maps of the S0, S950, S1050 and S1150 samples respectively.

The citing text states that the S0 sample exhibits the most pronounced residual stress with an average KAM value of 1.62, and that solution treatment reduces the average KAM of S950, S1050 and S1150 to approximately 0.4.
The citing text states that the maximum average grain size of 32.0 µm is achieved at the highest solution temperature of 1150 °C.

The citing text states that S950 has the maximum densities of annealing twin boundaries (Σ3, 60°) and HAGBs, 0.146 and 0.114 µm/µm² respectively, decreasing to minima of 0.040 and 0.019 µm/µm² for S1150.

The citing text asserts that after solution treatment the S950, S1050 and S1150 samples show complete recrystallization characterized by abundant ATBs and HAGBs within equiaxed austenite grains — consistent with the red-dominated GB maps (b₂)–(d₂).

subfigures.description: IPF orientation map of S0 with 50 µm scale bar and an IPF colour triangle keyed to [001], [101], [111]. Bimodal grain structure: large grains with fine grains clustered at their interfaces.
KAM map of S0 with a 0°–5° colour bar and 50 µm scale bar. Mottled green/yellow regions with residual dark-blue areas indicate locally high misorientation/residual stress.
GB distribution map of S0, 50 µm scale bar; legend blue = 2–10°, red = >10°. A dense network of blue (LAGB) traces with fewer red (HAGB) lines.
IPF map of S950, 100 µm scale bar; fine, more uniform equiaxed grains with multi-coloured (random) orientations.
KAM map of S950, 0°–5° colour bar, 100 µm scale bar; nearly uniform dark blue, i.e. low misorientation.
GB map of S950, 100 µm scale bar; dense red (>10°) boundary network with straight twin segments and few blue LAGB lines.
IPF map of S1050, 100 µm scale bar; coarser equiaxed grains with several long straight twin bands inside grains.
KAM map of S1050, nearly uniform dark blue with only faint traces along boundaries.
GB map of S1050; sparse red HAGB traces outlining grains plus abundant straight parallel twin-boundary lines; very few blue LAGB lines.
IPF map of S1150, 100 µm scale bar; the coarsest grains of the series, with prominent straight annealing-twin lamellae in several grains.
KAM map of S1150; essentially uniform dark blue, the lowest misorientation of the four conditions.
GB map of S1150; the sparsest boundary network of the series, almost entirely red >10° lines with straight twin traces.
